h1: Clear versus cloudy wort in malt whisky
title: Clear Versus Cloudy Wort in Whisky | Craft Beer School
desc: How wort clarity shapes malt whisky new make: why clear wort is linked to fruity spirit, cloudy wort to nutty spirit and how to control it.
teaser: Distillers can steer spirit character before the yeast is even pitched. Wort clarity is one of the first levers.
standfirst: Two distilleries can use the same malt and the same stills and still make very different spirit. One of the reasons sits in the mash tun: how clear the wort is when it runs to the washback.
sections:
Clear wort runs from the mash tun bright, with very few solids. Cloudy wort carries fine particles of grain, protein and fatty material along with the sugar. Both ferment and both distil. But they tend to give different spirits. Distillers choose between them on purpose.

The pattern is widely accepted in the industry. Clear wort is linked with a lighter, fruitier, estery new make. Cloudy wort is linked with a heavier, nuttier, maltier or more cereal spirit. The difference is not night and day, but it is real enough that distilleries guard their run-off habits.

The main suspect is lipids, the fatty material from the grain. Yeast in a clear, low lipid wort tends to produce more esters, the compounds behind fruity aromas such as banana, pear and apple. Lipids in cloudy wort tend to suppress ester formation. Cloudy wort also carries grain particles that can add cereal and nutty notes through fermentation and distillation.

Fermentation length and the stills then shape what reaches the spirit. Clear wort combined with a long fermentation is a common route to a fruity new make. Our guide to fermentation length and its effect on new make covers that half of the story.

Clear wort comes from a gentle, patient mash tun:

  • Recirculate the first runnings back over the bed until they run bright before sending wort to the washback.
  • Run off slowly. A fast pull compacts the bed and drags fines through.
  • Keep the grist close to a good split, roughly 20% husk, 70% grits and 10% flour, so the bed filters well.
  • If you have rakes or knives, lift the bed gently and only when needed.

The floor detail: watch the sight glass on the run-off, not the clock. Once the wort clouds, slow down or recirculate. Our guide to milling grist for a distillery explains the sieve test behind the grist split.

Clear wort usually costs a little time and sometimes a little extract. Slow run-off and recirculation stretch the mash cycle. Some distillers find a cloudy run-off recovers slightly more sugar from the bed. Cloudy wort can also carry more yeast nutrients, which helps a vigorous fermentation.

So the choice is a balance between house style, throughput and yield. A distillery making a light, fruity spirit accepts slower mashes. One making a heavier, robust spirit may run cloudier and faster. Neither is wrong. The mistake is drifting between the two without noticing, which gives inconsistent new make from week to week.

Clarity is easy to judge by eye and hard to record. A simple habit helps. Hold a sample of first wort in a clear glass against a printed line of text and note whether you can read it, or use a turbidity meter if you have one. Record it with each mash, along with run-off time and gravity.

Over a few months you will see how clarity moves with grist, run-off rate and malt lot. Then you can line it up against sensory notes on the new make. That link between a mash tun habit and a flavour in the spirit is what turns a production log into a tool.

Heat brings its own twist. A slow, careful run-off in a hot plant means wort sits warm for longer before cooling, which gives bacteria more time. Clean run-off pipework and the underback well. Cool wort promptly once it leaves the tun. Clear wort that picks up an infection on the way to the washback has lost the point of being clear.

Steering spirit character from the mash tun, the washback and the still as one system is the craft of malt distilling. It is also where a guide like this runs out of room.

On one mash, recirculate until the wort runs bright and run off slowly. On the next, run off at your usual pace without recirculation. Keep everything else the same and keep the new make from each separately. Nose both side by side, cut to the same strength with water. Note which one smells fruitier.
faqs: Does clear wort make better whisky?
Not better, different. Clear wort is widely linked with a lighter, fruitier spirit and cloudy wort with a nuttier, heavier one.
Why does cloudy wort give a nuttier spirit?
Cloudy wort carries more grain solids and lipids. Lipids tend to reduce ester formation by the yeast. The solids can add cereal and nutty notes.
How do I get clearer wort from my mash tun?
Recirculate the first runnings until bright, run off slowly, keep a good grist split and lift the bed gently if you have rakes.
It can cost a little time and sometimes a little extract, because slower run-off and recirculation stretch the mash cycle.
